newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds extend losses, spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds extend losses, spreads widen.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities continued their selloff from late Tuesday as yield spreads widened over their Treasury counterparts, traders said.
"We're widening out here," said one mortgage trader in New York. He attributed the slippage in spreads to heavy mortgage banker selling and some dumping of Ginnie Mae paper.
By late Wednesday, prices of pass-throughs were off 2/32 to 7/32 overall, while comparable Treasuries were down 3/32 to 7/32.

"I heard about people selling Ginnies, 7.5s and stuff like that," said another mortgage expert. "Spreads look like they're getting wider. I think people are just afraid to own something another point underwater," he said.
In Key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent issues were 6/32 lower, at 100-26/32, yielding 120 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was off 6/32 as well, at 100-24/32 and 100-30/32, respectively.
The five-year Treasury note was down 3/32 at 98-08/32 to yield 6.67 percent, while the 10-year Treasury note was off 7/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended an early close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT Thursday for U.S. credit markets, and a full close on Friday.
